'''Tamas Peter Brody''' (18 April 1920 – 18 September 2011) was a British-naturalised [[physicist]] and the [[co-inventor]] of [[active matrix]] [[thin-film transistor]] display technology together with Fang-Chen Luo,<ref name="IEEE">[https://web.archive.org/web/20130912052239/http://www.ieee.org/about/news/2011/honors_ceremony/releases_nishizawa.html 2011 IEEE Nishizawa Medal]</ref> having produced the world's first [[active-matrix liquid-crystal display]] (AM-LCD) in 1972 and the first functional AM-EL ([[electroluminescent display]]) in 1973 while employed by [[Westinghouse Electric Corporation]] in Pittsburgh. Brody coined the term "active matrix" and first used it in a published journal article in 1975.<ref name=OEDActiveMatrix>{{cite web|title=Active Matrix|year=2011|work=[[OED]]|publisher=[[Oxford University Press]]|url=http://www.oed.com/viewdictionaryentry/Entry/1953#eid19485882}}{{subscription required}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Brody|first1=T.P.|first2=Fang Chen |last2=Luo|last3=Szepesi |first3=Z. P. |last4=Davies |first4=D.H.|title=A 6 × 6-in 20-lpi electroluminescent display panel|journal=IEEE Transactions on Electron Devices|date=1 September 1975|volume=22|issue=9|pages=739–748|doi=10.1109/T-ED.1975.18214|bibcode=1975ITED...22..739B |s2cid=1378753 }}</ref>

==Early life and career==
Brody was born in Budapest, Hungary. From early childhood Brody was interested in sports, particularly swimming and rowing, and had a passion for [[classical music]].<ref name=Post-Gazette>{{cite news |title=Obituary: Thomas P. Brody / Made historic mark on electronics while living here |url=http://www.post-gazette.com/pg/11267/1177184-122-0.stm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110930112617/http://www.post-gazette.com/pg/11267/1177184-122-0.stm |url-status=dead |archive-date=30 September 2011 |newspaper=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]] |date=24 September 2011 |access-date=9 October 2011}}</ref> In 1938 he left his parents and two younger brothers behind in Hungary to learn the family trade at the [[London College of Printing]]. He was naturalised as a British subject in January 1948.<ref>{{cite news|title=NATURALISATION|url=http://www.london-gazette.co.uk/issues/38207/pages/1040|access-date=17 October 2011|newspaper=The London Gazette|date=13 February 1948}}</ref> He served as a designer/draftsman and worked for the [[Special Operations Executive]] in the [[British Army]] during and after the [[Second World War]], rising to the rank of staff captain.<ref>{{cite web|title=Piece reference HS 9/214|url=http://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/catalogue/displaycataloguedetails.asp?CATLN=6&CATID=8304658&j=1|work=Special Operations Executive: Personnel Files (PF Series)|publisher=The National Archives|access-date=17 October 2011}}</ref>

Brody studied [[piano]] at the [[Guildhall School of Music and Drama]] in [[London]] winning the Lady Mayoress' Prize for piano performance in 1952.<ref name=GSMD>{{cite web|title=Concert Programme CLA/056/AD/03/050|url=http://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/a2a/records.aspx?cat=075-cla056&cid=1-3#1-3|work=Guildhall School of Music and Drama|publisher=Corporation of London Records Office| access-date=17 October 2011}}{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> Brody met his future wife Maude M. Frost at a [[Fabian Society]] dance in London and they married in 1952.

Brody obtained a Ph.D. in [[Theoretical physics|Theoretical Physics]] from the [[University of London]] in 1953 and worked as a senior lecturer at the university until 1959. He moved to Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, on being offered the opportunity to work as a researcher for [[Westinghouse Electric Corporation]].<ref name="SID91">{{cite web|title=Thomas Peter Brody, SID Fellow and Display Pioneer, dies at 91|url=http://www.sid.org/IndustryNews/tabid/300/EntryId/13/Thomas-Peter-Brody-SID-Fellow-and-Display-Pioneer-dies-at-91.aspx|work=Society for Information Display|access-date=6 October 2011}}</ref>

From 1959 to 1979 he did theoretical work on [[tunnel diode]]s, [[semiconductor]] device theory and experiment, injection luminescence, [[field emission]], [[pattern recognition]], later turning his interest to [[thin film]] technology.<ref name="SID91"/><ref>{{cite journal|last=Brody|first=T. P.|title=Nature of the Valley Current in Tunnel Diodes|journal=Journal of Applied Physics|date=1 January 1962|volume=33|issue=1|pages=100–111|doi=10.1063/1.1728464|bibcode=1962JAP....33..100B }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Binary Material Field Emitter Structure|url=http://patft.uspto.gov/netacgi/nph-Parser?Sect2=PTO1&Sect2=HITOFF&p=1&u=%2Fnetahtml%2FPTO%2Fsearch-bool.html&r=1&f=G&l=50&d=PALL&RefSrch=yes&Query=PN%2F3720856|work=United States Patent 3,720,856|publisher=USPTO|access-date=17 October 2011}}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Reitboeck|first1=H.|last2=Brody|first2=T.|title=A transformation with invariance under cyclic permutation for applications in pattern recognition|journal=[[Information and Control]]|date=1 August 1969|volume=15|issue=2|pages=130–154|doi=10.1016/S0019-9958(69)90387-8|doi-access=}}</ref>

Brody died in Pittsburgh, aged 91.

==Thin-film transistors==
{{Quotation|The cathode ray tube, like the brontosaurus, will become extinct, and for the same reason: too much bulk, very little brain.|T. P. Brody, 1979<ref>{{cite journal|last=Brody|first=T. P.|title=When – If ever – Will the CRT be replaced by a flat display panel?|journal=Microelectronics Journal|date=1 May 1980|volume=11|issue=3|pages=5–9|doi=10.1016/S0026-2692(80)80089-9}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Westinghouse Wasn't Sure; Peter Brody Is|url=http://www.inc.com/magazine/19810601/9307.html|magazine=[[Inc. (magazine)|Inc.]]|date=June 1981 |access-date=6 October 2011}}</ref>}}

Over the years 1968–79, Brody developed many electronic uses for [[thin-film transistor]]s, including flexible circuits, aircraft power controls, industrial timers and others.<ref>{{cite book|editor-last=Crawford|editor-first=Gregory P.|title=Flexible flat panel displays|year=2005|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|location=Chichester, West Sussex, England|isbn=978-0-470-87048-8|pages=263|url=http://eu.wiley.com/WileyCDA/WileyTitle/productCd-0470870486.html}}</ref> His work at Westinghouse culminated in the invention of active matrix technology, using a [[CdSe]] [[thin-film transistor|TFT]] to drive each individual [[pixel]] of a [[flat-panel display]].<ref>{{US patent|US3840695A|US patent US3840695A: Liquid crystal image display panel with integrated addressing circuitry (10 October 1972)}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Brody|first=T.P.|author2=Asars, J.A. |author3=Dixon, G.D. |title=A 6 × 6 inch 20 lines-per-inch liquid-crystal display panel|journal=IEEE Transactions on Electron Devices|date=1 November 1973|volume=20|issue=11|pages=995&ndash;1001|doi=10.1109/T-ED.1973.17780|bibcode=1973ITED...20..995B }}</ref><ref name=Castellano>{{cite book|last=Castellano|first=Joseph A.|title=Liquid gold : the story of liquid crystal displays and the creation of an industry|url=https://archive.org/details/liquidgoldstoryl00cast|url-access=limited|year=2005|publisher=World Scientific|location=New Jersey [u.a.]|isbn=978-981-238-956-5|pages=[https://archive.org/details/liquidgoldstoryl00cast/page/n188 176]|edition=[Online-Ausg.]}}</ref><ref name="IEEE" /> This form of [[liquid-crystal display]] is the dominant technology in flat-panel displays.<ref>{{cite book|last=Boer|first=Willem den|title=Active matrix liquid crystal displays|year=2005|publisher=Elsevier|location=Amsterdam|isbn=978-0-7506-7813-1}} Preface.</ref>

When Westinghouse cancelled the research program in 1979, Brody resigned, and two years later founded Panelvision Corporation, the world's first [[AM-LCD]] company. In 1983 the company introduced the first AM-LCD products into the US market.<ref name=HCHSI>{{cite web|title=Panelvision MiniGraphic "active matrix" display|url=http://dssmhi1.fas.harvard.edu/emuseumdev/code/emuseum.asp?style=text&currentrecord=1&page=seealso&profile=objects&searchdesc=Related%20to%20Panelvision%20Corp...&searchstring=seealsoid/,/is/,/2382/,/false/,/true&sessionid=E0AB8FDF-5FA8-4C9E-A1D8-91A3EB4E1D16&action=searchrequest&style=single&currentrecord=1|work=Harvard's Collection of Historical Scientific Instruments|access-date=6 October 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120401210932/http://dssmhi1.fas.harvard.edu/emuseumdev/code/emuseum.asp?style=text&currentrecord=1&page=seealso&profile=objects&searchdesc=Related%20to%20Panelvision%20Corp...&searchstring=seealsoid%2F%2C%2Fis%2F%2C%2F2382%2F%2C%2Ffalse%2F%2C%2Ftrue&sessionid=E0AB8FDF-5FA8-4C9E-A1D8-91A3EB4E1D16&action=searchrequest&style=single&currentrecord=1|archive-date=1 April 2012|df=dmy-all}}</ref> Panelvision was acquired by Litton Systems in 1985, and after a period of consulting, Dr. Brody founded Magnascreen Corporation, oriented towards very large area displays, in 1988. This venture was funded in part by [[Jerome Wiesner]], Richard Leghorn of [[Itek]], and [[Apple Inc.|Apple]]'s [[John Sculley]], and won contracts worth $7.8 million from the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency ([[DARPA]]).<ref>{{cite journal|last=Florida|first=Richard|author2=Browdy, David |title=The invention that got away|journal=Technology Review|date=August–September 1991|volume=94|issue=6|pages=42–55|url=https://docs.google.com/viewer?a=v&pid=explorer&chrome=true&srcid=0B0wA-3C6mGX4MjlhNWMzNGMtMzgxNC00NWE3LWIyYmEtNDNjZjQ4M2ZjNmMx&hl=en_GB|access-date=11 October 2011}}</ref>

Brody left Magnascreen in 1990 to form Active Matrix Associates, a consulting group, and over the period 1991–97 worked on a number of classified projects for DARPA. In 1998, in collaboration with two former Westinghouse colleagues, Bob Stapleton and Paul Malmberg, he invented a process for fabricating low-cost thin film electronic circuits by purely [[additive manufacturing|additive processes]]. In 2002 he founded Amedeo Corporation (now Advantech US<ref>{{cite web|title=Advantech US|url=http://www.advantechus.com|work=Corporate website|access-date=12 October 2011}}</ref>), funded in part by [[Compaq]], dedicated to the exploitation of additive technology. The company is concentrating on the development and commercial production of low cost active matrix [[backplane]]s for emerging display technologies, including [[AM-OLED]]. He was active as chief scientist of Advantech US until his death at the age of 91.

[[File:TPBrody.jpg|thumb|Brody in 2008]]
Brody was a [[fellow]] of the [[Society for Information Display]] (SID), and a recipient of many awards in recognition of his pioneering work, which became the foundation of a major new industry. He published over 70 scientific papers and received more than 60 patents.<ref name="SID91"/> The SID created the Peter Brody Prize in 2017 to honor outstanding contributions of young researchers to active matrix information display technology.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sid.org/Awards/Individual-Honors-and-Awards/Peter-Brody|access-date=25 August 2025|title=Peter Brody Prize|publisher=[[Society for Information Display]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://uk.finance.yahoo.com/news/sid-announces-peter-brody-prize-000432407.html|title=SID Announces New Peter Brody Prize to Honor Young Researchers for Outstanding Contributions for Active Matrix Addressed Information Displays|access-date=2017-05-10|language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
*1976 – [[Society for Information Display]] (SID) Special Recognition Award<ref>{{cite web|title=Special Recognition Awards|url=http://65.38.182.180/AboutSID/Awards/IndividualHonorsandAwards/SpecialRecognition.aspx|work=Awards|publisher=Society for Information Display|access-date=12 October 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120708094443/http://65.38.182.180/AboutSID/Awards/IndividualHonorsandAwards/SpecialRecognition.aspx|archive-date=8 July 2012}}</ref>
*1983 – SID Fellowship<ref name="SID91" />
*1987 – [[SID Karl Ferdinand Braun Prize]]<ref name="SID91" />
*1988 – [[Rank Prize in Optoelectronics]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Rank Prize for Optoelectronics|url=http://www.rankprize.org/opto-electronics1.htm|work=Prizes awarded by the Optoelectronics Fund|publisher=Rank Prize|access-date=12 October 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029194700/http://www.rankprize.org/opto-electronics1.htm|archive-date=29 October 2013}}</ref> (UK)
*1988 – [[Eduard Rhein Foundation|Eduard Rhein Prize]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Award Winners (chronological)|url=http://www.eduard-rhein-stiftung.de/html/Preistraeger_e.html|work=Award Winners|publisher=Eduard Rhein Foundation|access-date=12 October 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110718233021/http://www.eduard-rhein-stiftung.de/html/Preistraeger_e.html|archive-date=18 July 2011}}</ref> (Germany)
*2011 – [[IEEE Jun-ichi Nishizawa Medal]]<ref name="IEEE" />
*2012 – [[Charles Stark Draper Prize]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Draper Prize 2012|url=http://www.draperprize.org/2012.php|work=Draper Prize|publisher=National Academy of Engineering|access-date=6 January 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120314095934/http://www.draperprize.org/2012.php|archive-date=14 March 2012|df=dmy-all}}</ref>

Brody was the first person in history to receive all three major SID awards.
